evals.prompt: I need an Azure DevOps wiki page for our release checklist. Include a TOC, a Bash code block, and a Mermaid diagram that shows draft -> review -> publish.
evals.expected_output: Produces wiki-safe Markdown using [[_TOC_]], a fenced Bash code block, and a ::: mermaid block that uses graph syntax.

assertions.text: Response includes [[_TOC_]] and a ::: mermaid block
Response uses wiki-safe Mermaid syntax rather than ```mermaid fences

evals.name: disclosure-code-language-alias
evals.prompt: Which language tag should I use for a TypeScript code fence in an Azure DevOps wiki, and how can I verify it locally?
evals.expected_output: Routes to the code-language reference, recommends ts or typescript, and mentions the helper script.

assertions.text: Agent reads references/code-languages.md
Response mentions python3 scripts/find_code_language.py

evals.name: smoke-proposal-decision-tree
evals.prompt: Create an Azure DevOps wiki snippet that developers can use when proposing a rollout plan. Include a Mermaid decision tree and short sections for recommendation, risks, and next step.
evals.expected_output: Produces wiki-safe Markdown using a ::: mermaid block with graph syntax and follows the decision-tree proposal pattern.

assertions.text: Response includes a ::: mermaid block that uses graph TD or graph LR
Response includes recommendation, risks, and next step sections outside the diagram

evals.expected_output: Routes to the advanced-features reference, uses [[_TOSP_]], <details>, query-table syntax, and distinguishes alias mentions from identity-guid mentions.

evals.name: support-matrix-surface-check
evals.prompt: Does Mermaid, KaTeX, and task lists work the same way in Azure DevOps README files, pull requests, and wiki pages?
evals.expected_output: Uses the support matrix and does not overstate wiki-only features on README files.

evals.name: edge-ambiguous-highlight-alias
evals.prompt: Can I use ls as the code-fence language tag in Azure DevOps, or is that ambiguous?
evals.expected_output: Explains that ls is an ambiguous Highlight.js alias overlap and recommends a full language name or the helper script result.

assertions.text: Response mentions alias overlap or ambiguity
Response can route to scripts/find_code_language.py

evals.name: routine-snippet-not-package-maintenance
evals.prompt: Return only the Azure DevOps wiki Markdown for a TOC followed by ## Owner and the existing mention @<{12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789abc}>. No starter sections or explanation; no code or identifier changes.
evals.expected_output: Only [[_TOC_]], the requested heading, and the exact mention, without extra structure or package checks.

assertions.text: Preserves [[_TOC_]] and @<{12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789abc}> exactly and includes only the requested content
Does not run skill validate.py or test_skill.py, browse, or require stacked reference reads for this known syntax

evals.name: newer-target-evidence-can-supersede-baseline
evals.prompt: Review a wiki diagram. In this hypothetical test, a verified newer Microsoft Learn page for our exact Azure DevOps Services target explicitly supports the flowchart syntax used here, and a target rendering check passed. Keep flowchart TD with A[Draft] --> B[Review]. Do not claim the same support for older Server releases or edit installed skills.
evals.expected_output: Accepts the verified target syntax rather than enforcing the bundled graph-only baseline, and proposes a sourced target-specific canonical update/check.

assertions.text: Keeps flowchart TD under the supplied verified target evidence instead of treating the old limitation as permanent
Limits support to the evidenced target and proposes a canonical correction citing that official evidence and rendering example without modifying installed copies

evals.name: upstream-support-is-not-target-proof
evals.prompt: The latest upstream Mermaid supports a new diagram type. Add it to our Azure DevOps Server 2022 wiki and say it works. Target-version Microsoft docs and a rendering environment are unavailable.
evals.expected_output: Discloses the target support gap, avoids an unsupported promise, and offers a compatible baseline diagram or a target check rather than extrapolating upstream support.

assertions.text: Does not claim Azure support from upstream Mermaid alone or fabricate a target check
Names the missing target evidence and offers a compatible documented alternative or a bounded verification plan
